terms.gloss: deus ex machina; an outside authority intervening to resolve complex disputes
terms.why_hard: Literal translation loses the play on both theatrical trope and computer hardware/code metaphor.

proposed.ja: デウス・エクス・マキナ（機械仕掛けの神）

terms.gloss: checks and balances (used metaphorically for forum community politics)
terms.why_hard: Usually political jargon, here applied internally to social community management.

terms.gloss: Supreme moderator / head administrator of the forum
terms.why_hard: Mock-grandiose title mixing administrative tech role with sovereign authority.

terms.gloss: Ilya Perekopsky, Durov's university friend and future deputy CEO of VKontakte
terms.why_hard: Must match standard transliteration of key historical figure in early VK history.

terms.gloss: The Matrix (1999 sci-fi movie)
terms.why_hard: Quotation style and iconic movie naming across languages.

terms.gloss: cast a spell/illusion/haze over people to keep them deceived
terms.why_hard: 'Морок' is archaic/folklore-tinged Russian for fog, delusion, or hypnotic trance.

terms.gloss: Morpheus, character from The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Russian transliteration of Greek/Matrix character name.

terms.gloss: The Oracle (Pythia) from The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Russian Matrix dub translates 'The Oracle' as 'Пифия' (Pythia), unlike English original.

proposed.ja: オラクル（預言者ピュティア）

terms.gloss: to code / write software
terms.why_hard: Informal developer slang in 2000s Russian internet culture.

terms.gloss: "Wake up, Neo. You are the Chosen One" (paraphrased line/trope from The Matrix)
terms.why_hard: Iconic catchphrase whose exact wording differs across localized dubs.

proposed.en: "Wake up, Neo. You are the One"
proposed.ja: 「起きろ、ネオ。お前が選ばれし者だ」

terms.gloss: the Construct / white loading program space in The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Visual allusion to the white void scene in the movie.

proposed.ja: 白い空間（コンストラクト）

terms.gloss: Keanu Reeves, actor playing Neo in The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Standard transliteration in target languages.

terms.gloss: Durov's handle / nickname (Totem) on university forums and IRC
terms.why_hard: Could be mistranslated as a generic noun ('a totem') rather than Durov's forum handle.

terms.gloss: pomp, grandiosity, self-importance, drama, high rhetorical drama
terms.why_hard: Russian 'пафос' has a broader colloquial connotation of self-dramatizing gravitas than English 'pathos'.

proposed.ja: 壮大なドラマ性と威厳

terms.gloss: Malcolm X, American civil rights activist
terms.why_hard: Spelling of the iconic figure's name.

terms.gloss: crafting/fashioning a persona or public image
terms.why_hard: Colloquial use of 'лепить' gives an artisanal, deliberate construction feeling.

proposed.ja: ペルソナ（仮面）を作り上げる

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov's early personal website / repository for students
terms.why_hard: Specific historic domain name; must remain exact.

terms.gloss: "Morals and Dogma of the Ancient and Accepted Scottish Rite of Freemasonry" by Albert Pike
terms.why_hard: Shortened Russian title refers to Pike's 1871 classic Masonic book 'Morals and Dogma'.

proposed.zh: 阿尔伯特·派克的《道德与教条》
proposed.ja: アルバート・パイクの『モラルズ・アンド・ドグマ（道徳と教条）』

terms.gloss: to sweat it, stress out, or fuss over something
terms.why_hard: Everyday youth slang; overly formal rendering kills the casual tone.

terms.gloss: Saint Petersburg State University departmental / faculty web forums
terms.why_hard: Refers specifically to individual SPbGU academic department online bulletin boards.

proposed.ja: 学部ごとのフォーラム

terms.gloss: The unified university web forum created by Pavel Durov for SPbGU students
terms.why_hard: Exact historic web portal domain name.

terms.gloss: make a visual impact / launch a visual offensive (via posters)
terms.why_hard: Militaristic marketing metaphor used by Durov.

proposed.ja: 視覚的インパクトを与える

terms.gloss: the falling green digital rain / binary code from The Matrix
terms.why_hard: Direct visual reference to iconic Matrix digital rain motif.

proposed.ja: 緑色のバイナリコード

terms.gloss: Quote from Malcolm X's fiery speeches Durov was listening to while designing posters
terms.why_hard: Must be recognized as an excerpt from Malcolm X's radical rhetoric translated into Russian, not Durov's original words.

proposed.en: "It's time for Black people to pay America back"
proposed.zh: “是时候让黑人报复美国这310年的奴役了”
proposed.ja: 「黒人がアメリカに310年の奴隷制の報いを受けさせる時が来た」

terms.gloss: Russian school graduation medal: gold (only straight top grades) or silver; carries university admission privileges
terms.why_hard: A literal 'silver medal' loses that this is a nationally standardized academic award, not a contest prize

terms.gloss: Colloquial abbreviation of the mathematics-and-mechanics faculty of St Petersburg State University
terms.why_hard: Must be rendered as an insider nickname, not expanded as a full official name

terms.gloss: Japanese philology department, a philology-faculty specialization
terms.why_hard: Not 'Japanese literature' but a full philological program; keep as a program name for consistency with chapter 2's philology setting

terms.gloss: Amateur student-run performing arts (skits, plays) at Soviet/post-Soviet schools
terms.why_hard: Has no English one-word equivalent; 'amateur performance' misses the school-skit tradition connotation

terms.gloss: A morning variety show/party event typical of Russian schools
terms.why_hard: Often mistranslated as 'morning performance' without the school-festive register

terms.gloss: Russian version of 'Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?'
terms.why_hard: Must match the official local title, which differs from the US show name

proposed.en: Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?

terms.gloss: All the classes of one grade/cohort year (the whole year group)
terms.why_hard: School jargon; 'parallel' literally would be nonsense in English

terms.gloss: Elected/appointed class monitor, a distinct Soviet-school institution
terms.why_hard: Not 'president' or 'leader'; the class monitor role needs a consistent label across the book

terms.gloss: 'Common pot' — shared pooled money/collective action for all classmates
terms.why_hard: Idiom; literal 'common cauldron' obscures the pooled-money meaning

terms.gloss: Sheep/herd insult: Durov frames collective action as mindless flock behavior
terms.why_hard: The herd metaphor recurs through the book as Durov's anti-conformism motif; must keep sheep+herd pairing

proposed.en: You sheep... submit like the whole herd
proposed.zh: 你们这群羊……跟整个羊群一起

terms.gloss: Petrogradskaya Storona, a historic district of St Petersburg on the Petrograd side of the Neva
terms.why_hard: Standard district name; must be consistent with other St Petersburg geography in the book

proposed.zh: 彼得格勒区（彼得城一侧）

terms.gloss: Nickname of a classmate of Durov
terms.why_hard: A moniker whose real name and spelling must be checked against other segments; transliteration choice affects consistency

terms.gloss: Durov's Gymnasium 1996 classmate, later a well-known figure; recurring in the book
terms.why_hard: Recurring person; transliteration must match later segments

terms.gloss: Classmate surname
terms.why_hard: Recurring name; transliteration standardization

terms.gloss: Classmate surname
terms.why_hard: Recurring name; transliteration standardization

terms.gloss: Astronomers' daughter, Durov's main school debating partner
terms.why_hard: Recurring person across segments; surname form is Czech-style feminine

terms.gloss: Youth slang of the 2000s: 'held forth', 'envisioned/dreamed out loud', 'mocked a bit'
terms.why_hard: The author's stylized 2000s youth lexicon; a formal register would flatten the voice; must keep consistent slang tone

proposed.zh: 高谈阔论 / 展望畅想 / 调侃了一通
proposed.ja: 語り出した／将来像を語った／からかった

terms.gloss: Durov's self-declared goal: to become a 'totem', then an 'internet totem' — an object of collective veneration online
terms.why_hard: The book's key motif; 'totem' must be kept literal and consistent everywhere it recurs, not smoothed into 'icon' or 'leader'

proposed.ja: トーテム／インターネットのトーテム

terms.gloss: A spot in the school building nicknamed 'the Captain's Bridge' (lit. ship's bridge)
terms.why_hard: Both a place nickname and a pun on ship command; must be rendered as a fixed landmark name

terms.gloss: The corridor nicknamed 'the School' in the university building
terms.why_hard: A quoted nickname inside a university, not the school itself; careless translation reads as ordinary 'school'

terms.gloss: Lecture room 215, nicknamed 'Eurasia'
terms.why_hard: Serves as a section anchor; the nickname should be preserved, not expanded

terms.gloss: Philology faculty / Oriental studies faculty of St Petersburg State University (abbreviated jargon)
terms.why_hard: Insider abbreviations recur throughout the book; must be translated consistently as faculty names

proposed.en: the philology and Oriental studies faculties

terms.gloss: International Student Identity Card, ubiquitous on Russian campuses in the 2000s
terms.why_hard: Keep the ISIC acronym or the reference to a period document is lost

terms.gloss: Student slang: 'tails' = unpassed exam debts; 'dvechniki' = failing students
terms.why_hard: Both are invariable Russian university slang; literal 'tails' is meaningless but the joke notice needs equivalent playful register

proposed.ja: 単位の未取得（落とし科目）／落第生

terms.gloss: A student 'aesthetics and design' contest named 'Olympus' sponsored by beauty brands
terms.why_hard: The 'Olymp' name plays on Mount Olympus/ideal of beauty; sets up a scene central to Chapter 2 and must stay consistent

proposed.en: the 'Olympus' student beauty and design contest
proposed.zh: “奥林波斯”学生美学与设计大赛
proposed.ja: 「オリンポス」学生美とデザインコンテスト

terms.gloss: Sponsor logos on the poster: fashion magazine, cosmetics brand, mid-market Italian clothing brand
terms.why_hard: Brand names must be kept verbatim; they signal the event's consumerist tone of 2000s campus life

terms.gloss: The economics faculty of St Petersburg State University, where Durov goes flyering.
terms.why_hard: Informal abbreviation; must be kept distinct from филфак and rendered consistently as 'the economics faculty'.

terms.term: «Бог без машины: Истории 20 сумасшедших, сделавших в России бизнес с нуля»
terms.gloss: Kononov’s book about twenty unconventional founders who built businesses from scratch in Russia; its title plays on “deus ex machina.”
terms.why_hard: A literal title loses the pun on the theatrical phrase “God from the machine,” while “сумасшедших” is admiringly provocative.

proposed.en: God Without the Machine: Stories of 20 Madmen Who Built Businesses from Scratch in Russia
proposed.zh: 《没有机器的神：20个疯子在俄罗斯白手起家的故事》
proposed.ja: 『機械なき神――ロシアでゼロから事業を築いた20人の狂人たち』

terms.gloss: Twitter, the social-networking and microblogging service now called X.
terms.why_hard: The historical name and lowercase Russian usage should be preserved rather than updated to X.

terms.gloss: Mark Zuckerberg, founder of Facebook and a frequent counterpart to Durov in the book.
terms.why_hard: His full name may be needed for readers encountering the surname without Russian context.

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte and the central subject of the biography.
terms.why_hard: The inflected Russian surname must be normalized and transliterated consistently.

terms.gloss: Began behaving extravagantly, eccentrically, or outrageously.
terms.why_hard: It is colloquial and amused rather than a literal claim that he performed miracles or went mad.

terms.gloss: Russian 5,000-ruble notes, the country’s highest-denomination banknotes at the time.
terms.why_hard: Omitting the currency or denomination’s significance weakens the extravagance of the stunt.

terms.gloss: VKontakte’s headquarters in central St Petersburg.
terms.why_hard: Literally a command headquarters, it is used here for the company office and carries a quasi-military startup flavor.

terms.gloss: St Petersburg’s annual City Day celebration, observed around the anniversary of its founding.
terms.why_hard: It is a named municipal festival, not merely an unspecified day in the city.

proposed.ja: サンクトペテルブルク市の日

terms.gloss: Durov’s ironic characterization of throwing money into a crowd as an experiment in spontaneous civic organization.
terms.why_hard: A flat literal rendering can miss both the mock-scientific register and the satire of crowd behavior.

proposed.en: an impromptu experiment in citizens’ self-organization
proposed.zh: 一场关于市民自发组织的突发实验
proposed.ja: 市民の自己組織化をめぐる突発的な実験

terms.gloss: Deliberately provoked admirers or defenders of Stalin, chiefly online.
terms.why_hard: The internet verb implies baiting for reactions, while “Stalinists” denotes a specific ideological constituency.

proposed.zh: 在网上挑衅斯大林主义者
proposed.ja: スターリン主義者をネットで挑発した

terms.gloss: Naples, the city in southern Italy.
terms.why_hard: The Russian exonym must be mapped to each target language’s established place-name form.

terms.gloss: An international online dating and social discovery service founded by Andrey Andreev.
terms.why_hard: It should remain a brand name and be identified as a dating service rather than a generic website.

terms.gloss: Andrey Andreev, Russian-born technology entrepreneur and founder of Badoo.
terms.why_hard: His repetitive Russian name and surname require fixed transliteration and may otherwise look erroneous.

proposed.ja: アンドレイ・アンドレーエフ

terms.gloss: The mobile-phone or mobile-messaging product idea Durov was developing.
terms.why_hard: A literal “telephone idea” is unnatural and may obscure its likely connection to the project that became Telegram.

proposed.ja: 携帯向けサービスの構想

terms.gloss: LeWeb, a major European technology and internet conference.
terms.why_hard: The text calls it a festival, but it was a recognizable industry conference whose branding should be standardized.

terms.gloss: In a three-piece suit consisting of jacket, trousers, and waistcoat.
terms.why_hard: Russian тройка has several common meanings and here does not mean a trio, a grade, or a horse team.

proposed.ja: スリーピースのスーツ姿で

terms.gloss: Vladislav Tsyplukhin, VKontakte’s press secretary and public-relations figure.
terms.why_hard: The inflected surname requires normalization, and his role is needed to understand why Durov gave him this assignment.

terms.gloss: The Singer House on Nevsky Prospekt, which housed VKontakte’s headquarters.
terms.why_hard: It denotes a landmark building, not the Singer company or a person named Singer.

terms.gloss: A monochrome dog graphic used on the T-shirts distributed during the promotional stunt.
terms.why_hard: The image may be a specific campaign emblem or internet-culture reference rather than incidental decoration.

terms.gloss: Palace Square, the monumental central square of St Petersburg.
terms.why_hard: It has an established English name and substantial symbolic weight as the city’s principal public square.

terms.gloss: Durov’s cultivated imitation of Neo, the black-clad hacker hero of The Matrix.
terms.why_hard: Without recognizing the film allusion, it can be mistranslated as games literally played in or called “Neo.”

proposed.zh: 扮演《黑客帝国》里的尼奥
proposed.ja: 『マトリックス』のネオを気取ること

terms.gloss: Wet T-shirts, evoking sexualized wet-T-shirt contests or photo shoots.
terms.why_hard: The phrase carries a recognizable erotic-pop-culture association, not merely the fact that shirts became wet.

terms.gloss: Napoleon Hill, American self-help author best known for Think and Grow Rich.
terms.why_hard: The surname alone is ambiguous; the comparison points to motivational, success-manual rhetoric.

terms.gloss: Paul Graham, programmer, essayist, and co-founder of the startup accelerator Y Combinator.
terms.why_hard: The surname could refer to several Grahams; here it evokes aphoristic essays on startups, technology, and society.

terms.gloss: Old wineskins, from the biblical saying that new wine cannot be put into old wineskins.
terms.why_hard: Мехи here means skin containers, not fur or mechanical bellows, and the surrounding wine imagery depends on the Gospel allusion.

terms.gloss: Barack Obama, 44th US President running for re-election in 2012
terms.why_hard: Standard presidential name, but requires consistent formal rendering across languages.

terms.gloss: Campaign fundraising/financing
terms.why_hard: Often used in banking for liability funding; here it specifically refers to political fundraising.

terms.gloss: Doesn't understand / isn't clued into mobile tech
terms.why_hard: Colloquial 'не рубит' mixed with tech loanword 'мобайл' requires matching conversational register.

terms.gloss: Jim Messina, campaign manager for Obama's 2012 re-election campaign
terms.why_hard: Transliteration of an American political strategist's name.

terms.gloss: Political strategist / campaign manager
terms.why_hard: Post-Soviet term carries connotations of cynical media manipulation, but here applied to an American campaign strategist.

terms.gloss: Larry Page, co-founder of Google
terms.why_hard: Standard transliteration, must match conventional tech spelling.

terms.gloss: Internet visionaries / tech industry luminaries
terms.why_hard: Hyphenated loanword phrase; needs an idiomatic corporate/tech equivalent.

proposed.ja: インターネット界の重鎮

terms.gloss: Offline social network / grassroots ground game network
terms.why_hard: Combines digital jargon with real-world political organizing; shouldn't sound like a contradiction in terms.

proposed.ja: オフラインのソーシャルネットワーク

terms.gloss: Multi-level marketing / network marketing pyramid structure
terms.why_hard: Acronym borrowed from English direct selling; needs recognizable market term.

proposed.ja: マルチレベル・マーケティング（MLM）

terms.gloss: To force oneself against one's nature / go against one's grain
terms.why_hard: Literal 'break oneself' sounds physical rather than psychological.

terms.gloss: To preach / evangelize / spread political messages passionately
terms.why_hard: Religious term used here metaphorically for persuasive modern political messaging.

terms.gloss: Social media is fundamentally all about these things
terms.why_hard: Calque of the English 'is all about...'; tone is colloquial 2010s digital marketing jargon.

proposed.en: social media is completely tailored to these things
proposed.zh: 社交媒体骨子里就是为这些而生的
proposed.ja: ソーシャルメディアはまさにそうした性質に合致している

terms.gloss: Casual snapshots / photos (affectionate diminutive)
terms.why_hard: Diminutive suffix '-очки' marks informal, domestic snapshot sharing online, not formal photos.

proposed.ja: ちょっとしたスナップ写真

terms.gloss: Twitter's historical 140-character limit
terms.why_hard: Historical period detail defining early Twitter before the limit doubled to 280.

proposed.ja: ツイッターの140文字制限

terms.gloss: Specific VKontakte features/tools for events, group chats, and doc collaboration
terms.why_hard: These are literal VK product feature names from the late 2000s/early 2010s, not generic descriptions.

proposed.zh: “活动”、“多人对话”、“协同文档”等功能
proposed.ja: 「イベント」「複数人チャット」「共同ドキュメント」などの機能

terms.gloss: Rorschach inkblot test, metaphor for blank slate / projection screen
terms.why_hard: Psychological reference to psychological projection, recurring metaphor for Durov's elusive persona.

proposed.ja: ロールシャッハ・テストのインクの染み

terms.gloss: To win over hearts and minds / captivate followers
terms.why_hard: Echoes biblical/Gospel motif of 'fishers of men' (ловцы человеческих душ).

terms.gloss: Quality of being a Rorschach test onto which people project their own desires
terms.why_hard: Neologism coined by the author from Rorschach; needs a matching inventive nominalization.

terms.gloss: Totem / symbolic figurehead / embodiment of a movement
terms.why_hard: Author's recurring mythologizing metaphor for Durov as an enigmatic figurehead.

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder and chief executive of VKontakte.
terms.why_hard: His surname must be transliterated consistently and not replaced by his full name indiscriminately.

terms.gloss: Vladislav Mirilashvili and Lev Leviev, VKontakte co-founders and shareholders close to Durov.
terms.why_hard: The familiar first names conceal identities established elsewhere and should not be translated as unidentified men.

terms.gloss: Twitter, the social-media platform on which Durov posted publicly.
terms.why_hard: The Russian text uses a lowercase genericized form, but target-language brand conventions differ.

terms.gloss: Durov's mocking public response to the prosecutor's office that had summoned him.
terms.why_hard: Прокуратура is Russia's state prosecution authority, not an individual prosecutor or merely 'the authorities.'

proposed.en: his response to the prosecutor's office

terms.gloss: An official summons requiring Durov to appear for questioning.
terms.why_hard: Depending on its legal status, it may be mistranslated as a subpoena, warrant, or ordinary invitation.

terms.gloss: Formal questioning by Russian investigators or prosecutors.
terms.why_hard: It can mean an official interrogation rather than a neutral interview.

terms.gloss: VKontakte's audience of many millions, imagined as political and negotiating weight behind Durov.
terms.why_hard: Rendering it as mere readership loses the implication of a mass constituency and source of power.

proposed.en: an audience of millions behind you
proposed.zh: 背后数以百万计的用户
proposed.ja: 背後にいる数百万のユーザー

terms.gloss: The Russian state portrayed as institutionally expert at coercing and crushing opponents.
terms.why_hard: Давить carries physical, political, and psychological pressure; a literal 'press' is too weak.

proposed.en: the state, whose specialty was coercion
proposed.zh: 一个最擅长施压的国家机器
proposed.ja: 圧力をかけることを本領とする国家

terms.gloss: A symbolic figure or object treated as a source of group identity and power, apparently referring to Durov or VK.
terms.why_hard: The referent depends on earlier context; translating it literally without identifying the metaphor may confuse readers.

terms.gloss: Vladislav Surkov, a senior Kremlin political strategist who later moved to the Russian government.
terms.why_hard: His role and informal influence matter more here than a bare surname suggests.

terms.gloss: The Russian presidential administration and its political power center, not merely the Moscow fortress.
terms.why_hard: A literal geographical rendering would miss its metonymic meaning as the presidency.

terms.gloss: An informal description of Surkov's government post overseeing modernization and technology policy.
terms.why_hard: It is deliberately colloquial rather than an official job title and should not be overformalized.

proposed.ja: 政府のテクノロジー担当責任者

terms.gloss: Vyacheslav Volodin, the Kremlin official who succeeded Surkov in overseeing domestic politics.
terms.why_hard: The surname alone assumes knowledge of a major Russian political operator and his relation to Surkov.

terms.gloss: Krestovsky Island, an affluent island district in Saint Petersburg where Durov had an apartment.
terms.why_hard: Readers may mistake it for a separate town and miss its elite residential connotations.

terms.gloss: Officers of OMON, Russia's militarized riot and special-purpose police.
terms.why_hard: Calling them ordinary police loses the force's intimidating, paramilitary associations.

terms.gloss: An earlier-mentioned monkey experiment used by Durov as a lesson about fear, attachment, or perceived ownership.
terms.why_hard: Its meaning depends on an earlier anecdote and cannot safely be expanded from this passage alone.

terms.gloss: VKontakte's in-house security service or Durov's private security personnel.
terms.why_hard: It could be mistaken for a state security agency such as the FSB.

terms.gloss: A sardonic Russian term for a theatrical armed raid by masked law-enforcement officers.
terms.why_hard: The literal 'mask show' is opaque and misses its post-Soviet association with intimidating police raids on businesses.

proposed.ja: 覆面武装警官による強制捜査

terms.gloss: VKontakte, the Russian social-networking service founded by Durov.
terms.why_hard: Its name, abbreviation, and platform terminology must remain consistent throughout the book.

terms.gloss: Durov's 2.7 million VK followers or subscribers who received his posts.
terms.why_hard: Подписчики on VK may be rendered as subscribers or followers; the platform-specific choice must be consistent.

terms.gloss: Thomas Carlyle, the nineteenth-century Scottish writer and historian quoted by Durov.
terms.why_hard: The quotation may have an established English original and established Chinese and Japanese translations.

terms.term: «Насколько человек побеждает страх, настолько он человек»
terms.gloss: A maxim attributed to Thomas Carlyle equating humanity with the degree to which one conquers fear.
terms.why_hard: A published source wording should be used if verifiable rather than retranslating the Russian paraphrase freely.

proposed.en: “A man is a man to the extent that he conquers fear.”
proposed.zh: “一个人战胜恐惧到什么程度，他就成为了什么程度的人。”
proposed.ja: 「人は恐怖に打ち勝つ度合いに応じて、人たりうる」

terms.gloss: The Russian ruling and law-enforcement apparatus viewed as one impersonal political system.
terms.why_hard: A literal 'system' can sound abstract; here it denotes the regime and its coercive machinery.

terms.gloss: Colloquial wording for police rounding up and arresting opposition protesters.
terms.why_hard: Вязать literally means 'tie up' or 'knit' but in police slang means seize or detain.

proposed.zh: 大肆抓捕反对派示威者
proposed.ja: 反体制派のデモ参加者を次々と拘束していた

terms.gloss: Saint Isaac's Square or the area by Saint Isaac's Cathedral in central Saint Petersburg.
terms.why_hard: The adjective omits the noun in colloquial usage, so the intended landmark or square must be supplied.

terms.gloss: Special police vans used to transport detainees and arrested protesters.
terms.why_hard: They are not ordinary vans or prison buses; the word has strong associations with protest arrests.

terms.gloss: Alexei Navalny, Russian opposition politician, lawyer, and anti-corruption activist.
terms.why_hard: His public role in 2011–2012 differs from his later international profile and should match the period.

proposed.ja: アレクセイ・ナワリヌイ

terms.gloss: A period-specific epithet presenting Navalny as a lawyer and anti-corruption campaigner.
terms.why_hard: Адвокат can mean a licensed attorney, while the compound epithet marks how he was publicly known at the time.

proposed.ja: 反汚職活動家の弁護士

terms.gloss: Navalny's crowdsourced project investigating suspected corruption in Russian public procurement.
terms.why_hard: The coined name puns on распил, slang for embezzling or carving up state funds.

terms.gloss: Navalny's volunteer network for spreading opposition and civic messages beyond the internet.
terms.why_hard: Its name jokingly reverses the notion of a state propaganda machine; bland literal wording loses the irony.

proposed.ja: 「善意のプロパガンダ・マシン」

terms.gloss: VKontakte's maximum permitted membership for a user-created group.
terms.why_hard: It is a platform capacity limit, not a restriction on how many people may use VK overall.

proposed.ja: グループの参加者数上限

terms.gloss: A figurative image whose immediate referent is Durov's head or mental world as he drives fear away.
terms.why_hard: The unusual phrase is context-dependent and may carry an earlier recurring image that a literal 'shining globe' obscures.

proposed.en: his gleaming globe of a head
proposed.ja: 彼の光る球体のような頭

terms.gloss: American Founding Fathers
terms.why_hard: must use standard historical epithet, not literal translation

proposed.ja: アメリカ建国の父たち

terms.gloss: libertarian state, political-philosophy term
terms.why_hard: libertarian has different connotations across cultures, must not be confused with 'liberal'

terms.gloss: urine-stinking underground pedestrian pass, grim Russian urban feature
terms.why_hard: conveys squalor and dereliction; needs vivid but not vulgar equivalent

terms.gloss: drug dealers (loanword drug + dealer)
terms.why_hard: keep colloquial register consistent with period slang

terms.gloss: cracking sunflower seeds, common idle habit of security guards/loiterers in Russia
terms.why_hard: culturally specific gesture signifying boredom/low status; literal translation may seem odd

proposed.ja: ヒマワリの種を齧っていた

terms.gloss: pseudo-classicist styled hotel, likely St Petersburg architecture reference
terms.why_hard: architectural style term needs consistent rendering, implies faux-grandeur contrast with squalor

proposed.zh: 仿古典主义风格的酒店
proposed.ja: 擬古典主義様式のホテル

terms.gloss: sleepwalkers - metaphor for the two exhausted interlocutors
terms.why_hard: must preserve dreamlike/exhaustion metaphor consistently

terms.gloss: ironic 'profound constitutional/stroll', mock-serious phrase for their late-night walk-and-talk
terms.why_hard: irony and archaic register ('моцион') easily lost

terms.gloss: Durov's self-described 'mystical thinking', a known quote/persona trait
terms.why_hard: needs to read as a direct quote consistent with public Durov mythology

terms.gloss: Lenta.ru, major Russian news website
terms.why_hard: proper noun of a news outlet, keep unadapted with .ru

terms.gloss: the 2011-2012 protest rallies in Russia (Bolotnaya-era)
terms.why_hard: specific historical protest wave; generic 'rallies' loses context

terms.gloss: reference to VKontakte closing/blocking opposition groups under political pressure
terms.why_hard: requires knowing VK's role in protest-era censorship controversy

terms.gloss: recurring theme phrase: fear accelerates the negative scenario
terms.why_hard: must render consistently as a thematic refrain

proposed.zh: 恐惧会加速负面的走向
proposed.ja: 恐怖はネガティブな筋書きを早める

terms.term: ветхие мехи прохудятся и вино выльется само
terms.gloss: biblical allusion 'old wineskins will burst and wine will pour out' (Matthew 9:17)
terms.why_hard: biblical reference must be recognizable, not literalized

proposed.en: the old wineskins will burst and the wine will spill out on its own
proposed.zh: 陈旧的皮囊终将破裂，酒自会流出
proposed.ja: 古い革袋は破れ、ぶどう酒はおのずと流れ出る

terms.gloss: breaking of the old/decrepit world - recurring 'ветхий' motif tied to biblical wineskin image
terms.why_hard: should echo same root word 'ветхий' as later wineskin metaphor for consistency

proposed.en: the breaking of the decrepit old world

terms.gloss: English term used in original as coined concept for business-driven social activism
terms.why_hard: kept in English in source; decide whether to keep untranslated across all languages

proposed.zh: 行动主义资本主义（activist capitalism）
proposed.ja: アクティビスト・キャピタリズム（activist capitalism）

terms.gloss: Sennaya Square area in St Petersburg, historically gritty district
terms.why_hard: place name with connotations of grime/crime, needs consistent transliteration

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, VKontakte founder
terms.why_hard: surname consistency across segments

terms.gloss: shift of information paradigm, tech-utopian framing
terms.why_hard: must stay consistent with other tech/ideology terms in book

terms.gloss: clarity of 4 a.m. - narrator's ironic epistemic marker
terms.why_hard: tone of exhausted-lucid irony must carry over

proposed.en: with all the clarity possible at four in the morning
proposed.zh: 以凌晨四点所能有的清醒
proposed.ja: 午前四時に可能な限りの明晰さで

terms.gloss: brown/rust-colored brick, likely referencing typical Soviet-era construction rubble
terms.why_hard: concrete visual detail of urban decay, keep consistent imagery

terms.gloss: 'suffer defeat' - recurring theme of failure due to lack of understanding vs calculation
terms.why_hard: consistency with 'умение считать/понимать' contrast elsewhere in Durov's philosophy quotes

terms.gloss: generic security guard figure, recurring type in Russian urban scenes symbolizing indifferent authority
terms.why_hard: tone: indifferent, low-level authority figure, not menacing

terms.gloss: speculative/abstract, Durov dismissing politics as merely theoretical
terms.why_hard: philosophical register word, must not flatten to 'theoretical' losing slight pejorative tone

terms.gloss: Russian tech/media news site covering internet business, where this feud played out in comments
terms.why_hard: Looks like a random URL; must stay as the named venue, not ‘a blog’

terms.gloss: Igor Ashmanov, well-known Russian internet entrepreneur and commentator on ads/search
terms.why_hard: Surname spelling (Ashmanov vs Ašmanov) must be fixed once

proposed.ja: イーゴリ・アシュマノフ

terms.gloss: Mail.ru Group, the portal/mail giant then trying to absorb VK
terms.why_hard: Later rebranded VK/VK Company; period name must stay Mail.ru

terms.gloss: Industry slang for display/banner (media) advertising inventory
terms.why_hard: Not ‘the media’; it’s buy-side jargon for display ads vs search

terms.gloss: A tame/in-house-favored ad agency kept on a leash by the brand’s ad department
terms.why_hard: прикормленное is ‘fed/tamed’, not merely ‘preferred’

proposed.ja: 飼いならされた広告代理店

terms.gloss: Media buyer in the agency chain
terms.why_hard: Keep as industry term, not ‘media purchaser’

terms.gloss: Media seller representing the publisher
terms.why_hard: Pair with media buyer; don’t collapse the chain

terms.gloss: Kickbacks paid up the advertising chain
terms.why_hard: Russian business slang, not ‘rollbacks’ of software

terms.gloss: Skimming/splitting the budget as ‘commissions’ along the chain
terms.why_hard: Literally ‘sawing up’; in 2000s RU business it means embezzlement of a contract

terms.gloss: Impressions actually delivered/spun for the client
terms.why_hard: Ad-ops slang; ‘spin’ of the counter, not ‘unscrewing’

proposed.ja: 消化インプレッション

terms.gloss: Portmanteau: skimming-plus-kickbacks endemic to display media
terms.why_hard: Coinage; don’t split into two ordinary words and lose the bite

terms.gloss: Contextual/search ads (Yandex Direct-style) with no agency chain
terms.why_hard: In RU 2010s this specifically contrasts with ‘медийка’, not all targeted ads

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, VK founder; surname used alone after first mention
terms.why_hard: Must match book-wide ‘Durov’, never ‘Duroff’

terms.gloss: VKontakte, the social network (later VK)
terms.why_hard: Period branding with quotes/Cyrillic; don’t silently modernize to VK everywhere

terms.gloss: Mail.ru’s public file-hosting service, a warez dump in Durov’s attack
terms.why_hard: Keep the hostname; ‘Mail.ru files’ loses the product identity

terms.gloss: Warez: pirated software/media dumps
terms.why_hard: Internet-piracy loanword; ‘contraband’ is too vague

terms.gloss: File-exchange/hosting sites of the late-2000s RU net
terms.why_hard: Also means currency exchangers; here it’s file lockers

terms.gloss: Durov’s insult: a tasteless warehouse of viruses and warez
terms.why_hard: безвкусный is ‘tasteless/kitschy’, not merely ‘unpalatable’

proposed.en: a tasteless warehouse of viruses and warez
proposed.zh: 毫无品位的病毒与盗版仓库
proposed.ja: 趣味のないウイルスとウェアズの倉庫

terms.gloss: Selectel, the Levov/Volochkov hosting/ISP later tied to VK infrastructure
terms.why_hard: Latin branding Selectel; don’t transliterate Selektel inconsistently

terms.gloss: Lev and Slava: Lev Leviev and Vyacheslav (Slava) Mirilashvili, VK co-owners
terms.why_hard: Diminutives; first names alone are opaque without the established pair

terms.gloss: Dmitry Grishin, then CEO of Mail.ru Group
terms.why_hard: Surname-only; must match earlier ‘Grishin’, not ‘Grishin/Grišin’ mix

terms.gloss: Durov’s put-down: ‘typical manager-speak’
terms.why_hard: менеджер in RU 2010s is a mild insult (corporate functionary), not ‘manager’ neutrally

proposed.ja: 典型的なマネージャー言葉

terms.gloss: Grishin’s jab: Durov has gotten carried away playing at show business and PR
terms.why_hard: заиграться is ‘gotten too into the game’, not simply ‘entered’ PR

proposed.en: gotten carried away with show business and PR
proposed.ja: ショービジネスとPR遊びに興じすぎた

terms.gloss: Totem, Durov/VK-related entity pouring profit into infrastructure (recurring in the book)
terms.why_hard: Looks like ‘totem’ the symbol; it is a company name that must stay consistent

terms.gloss: Pavel Durov, founder of VKontakte, the book's subject
terms.why_hard: Name must match the book-wide romanization; nothing locally hard

terms.gloss: Durov's associate walking with him in this passage
terms.why_hard: Unusual surname; must be romanized consistently across segments

terms.gloss: The tall third companion in the group that gets attacked
terms.why_hard: Long surname, easy to mistype inconsistently

terms.gloss: Durov referred to by a nickname/totemic epithet as he flees
terms.why_hard: A careless reader takes it as a random animal; it's a recurring epithet for Durov and must be rendered identically book-wide

terms.gloss: VKontakte headquarters (the office the guard didn't recognize Durov at)
terms.why_hard: Literally 'HQ/staff'; rendering as 'staff' (people) instead of 'headquarters' breaks the sense

terms.gloss: Subway sandwich chain restaurant
terms.why_hard: Russian transliteration of a Western brand; should be restored to the original brand name, not kept as 'Subvei'

Тверская: standardized as the proper street name rather than appending specific building context ('office').
